# Phase directive — "Version done-check" (Epoch 8, 0.1.0's last entry)

The operator's requests to the phase's orchestrator (the overseer, founder-delegated).

1. **Live sessions: up to 2 for this chunk** (the founder's own word, live, by dialog 2026-11-06 17:01Z). They are for
   `v1-53`'s one live `viola run` on Linux, plus one spare. They run on the headless pty rig, with no human key and no
   window. Ledger each start before it is made, with the clock's time.
2. **The 17 unclaimed capabilities are the FOUNDER's to rule, one by one** (his word, 2026-11-05, relayed: each is
   proved or deferred on his word): v1-01 · 03 · 04 · 05 · 07 · 09 · 10 · 11 · 13 · 21 · 24 · 26 · 27 · 34 · 35 · 36 ·
   53.
   - At P4, bring them to him as dialogs: per cap, prove (what this chunk does for it) or defer (with the reason),
     your recommendation first, each option's cost.
   - Group them at most four per dialog. Keep his questions apart from technical ones; the technical ones the
     overseer answers.
   - He may be away: a dialog then holds.
3. **A route split is his word too.** If the proved set will not fit one chunk, propose the split as a P4 question with
   its sizes.
4. **The entry's CARRYs are scope.** Among them:
   - **RUSTSEC-2026-0441:** move `portable-pty` off `=0.8.1` to a release whose graph drops `pin-utils`; no ignore
     widened. The `=0.8.1` pin's only reason, a Windows bug, left with the Windows code.
   - **v1-01's owner row.**
   - **The fd-inheritance measurement:** under the fake agent, the wrapped child's `/proc/<pid>/fd` holds no channel
     socket or listener.
   - **The `thiserror` census:** 10 measured against the masters' 9.
   - **The Windows remnants still in the code.**
   - **F434's two master edits.** Land them through the store's whole-fact form (`@fact id=… expect_rev=N
     whole=true`, rec v1.18, deployed): the seven directory-tree pointer lines removed from `fct-irhgihut`, and the
     obs `process-start` row `fct-yb5jpaot` at the header's 2 cells (`pty_backend` `openpty` alone, `sideload_fallback`
     gone). Then retire their CARRYs.
5. **The sampler stays unforced.** Keep every subagent and Workflow transcript.
6. **A dead draw follows the contract.** It takes one re-spawn, and then the contract decides; only `every draw dead`
   stops. **A tool fault stops the phase**, reported with the run dir and nothing patched.
7. **Standing:**
   - Read `df -h /tmp` before a stamped-home gate.
   - Health check 13's ⚠ for the removed `agent-run.ps1` is known upstream (F411): run no setup Phase 4 for it.
   - The Epoch 6–8 diagnoses and the code audit run ONCE at the version end, by the founder's word, so leave
     new-session's nudge unanswered.
8. **On the P5 card:** every refusal with the letter line you were following, and P5's `landed tx` line.

   - Read `claude --version` by path before each session (verification-harness.md 2026-10-10). Read the build's
     sha256 right before each session (verification-harness.md 2026-10-20).
   - Before each session: read `hyprctl locked` and the process census by `/proc/<pid>/exe` against this
     repository's root (host-linux.md 2026-10-07), and write one `start` row through `live-ledger.py` to
     `evidence/live-sessions.ndjson` (its `written_at` from the clock).
   - No key is typed into any dialog or the session, and the rig writes nothing to its pty before the stop. A start
     that meets any modal is killed with no key, recorded red and not re-fired. The round then stops for the
     operator.

9. **Live session 1: the verify** (`inputs#I3`). `target/debug/viola --home <vhome> verify -- <claude 2.1.287 by
   path>`, from the repository root as the 2026-10-19 round ran it. It ends `stamped 2.1.287  24 pass  0 fail` and
   leaves no `.viola-verify-*` dir. A red is recorded, never re-fired, and session 2 is not made.

10. **Live session 2: the wrapped start** (`inputs#I3`; v1-53, v1-27, CARRY 2, CARRY 11, CARRY 15).
    - Write `<vhome>/config.json` `{"v":1,"dialog_hold_s":3600}` (0600) before the start. Then run
      `target/debug/viola --home <vhome> run done-check -- <claude 2.1.287 by path>` under `live-pty.py`, with the
      cwd one 0700 dir under `…/priv/`.
    - **The start:** read `process-start{subject:"claude-child"}` with `cli_verified:true` and `pty_backend` `openpty`,
      and the start chain's product order `wheel` → `budget-gate` → `session-start` (obs-plan/span-trace-coverage
      fct-e6vtcesf).
    - **The child's fd table:** read `/proc/<child pid>/fd` of the real `claude` child. Record its fds and each one's
      target class, never a path: pty, socket, pipe, file under the home, other. The reading wanted is: fds 0–2 on
      `/dev/pts`, no `socket:` target that is viola's endpoint or listener, and no file under the home (CARRY 15's
      live table, beside E2).
    - **The hold:** the driver, unwrapped, with no `VIOLA_NAME`, sends one fixed prompt from `--file` asking the
      session to run one shell command that creates an empty file inside `…/priv/`. Wait for the `permission` line.
      Then neither answer nor type: the wrapper holds the dialog for 3600 s. Read `dialog-expired` (one line,
      `source: wrapper`), `dialog-answered{deadline_hit:true}` with its `duration_ms`, the hook's
      `hook-decision{decision_emitted:false, deadline_hit:false}`, and no human key in the meantime (the wheel
      record) (obs-plan/span-trace-coverage fct-k233iq5j).
    - **The killed-wrapper leg** (CARRY 11's real-claude leg): `kill -KILL <wrapper pid>`. Read the child gone by pid
      and start time within 10 s (architecture/established-decisions fct-44n3w6o5), with no
      `process-exit{subject:"self"}` written.
    - Then a `census` row: processes left 0. Write every reading to `evidence/live-round.md`, codes, counts and times
      only, and as ledger rows: `start` ×2, `reading` (kind · verdict), `census`.

11. **T3's witness** (`evidence/overseer-drive.md`; `inputs#I2` T3). Read this builder session's own wrapping
    through the installed product build. Record: `viola list --json`'s row for this instance (`wrapped:true`,
    `liveness:"live"`, read as booleans and words), and the instance's event kinds with their counts read through
    `jq` over its `events.ndjson`. The kinds wanted are: `send-issued`, `send-confirmed`, `prompt-submitted` with
    origin `driver`, and `link`. Record no text, id, path or time. This spends no live start.

12. **The CI read and the weekly run** (operator pass). The pushed sha's run is read job by job, all seven asserted
    green, `supply-chain` included. The last scheduled `nightly.yml` run is recorded: its conclusion and date (v1-01's
    «a weekly scheduled advisory run executes»).
- `tests/contract_config_keys.rs` — the closed config-key set and its no-redaction check (step 4)

- `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-06-version-done-check/evidence/` — `remnants.md`, `census.md`,
  `v1-09-amendments.md`, `v1-26-fix-pass.md`, the copied rig, `live-sessions.ndjson`, `live-round.md`,
  `overseer-drive.md`
- `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `deny.toml` — step 1
- `tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs` — step 5, only if no planted annotations case stands

- the 48 remnant files of research §Files to modify — step 2: `plain_drive @ src/cmd/mod.rs:309` (callers: its own
  file only) and the `EXE_SUFFIX` joins, no signature changed

- **The live round** (steps 8–10) runs once, by /implement, against real `claude`. It is no gate entry: its record is
  `evidence/live-sessions.ndjson` and `live-round.md`, which the reader entries below assert and which carry no
  `artifact` (the reader rule). A red in it is recorded and never re-fired.
- **The stamped-home entries** read `df -h /tmp` first (`inputs#I1` item 7).

- **No mutation entry:** the epoch-boundary audit owns `run --mutants` and runs once at the version end
  (`inputs#I1` item 7).

- **The diff is OS-sensitive by construction:** every Windows arm and path form leaves. So hygiene, push and the CI
  reads close the block, and the CI reads name the one leg left. `supply-chain` is now asserted green, where the last
  chunk recorded it as report-only.

- **The secret scan** runs in CI only, inside the `test` and `perf` jobs, which their reads assert (the last chunk's
  P5 measured the local scan past its bound).

  `verdict: green` on the pushed sha (per security-plan §Dependency Security; architecture §Established Decisions [PTY]).

- (remnants) The remnant probe entry exits 1 with no output, and `remnants.md` names every kept site with its reason
  (per architecture §Design Philosophy).

- (census) `tests/contract_os_gated_tests.rs` passes. `census.md` records the count by its rule, predicted 39 / 2 / 41
  (per test-plan §1 Test Scope Summary).

- (live) Exactly two starts are ledgered: one verify that ends `stamped 2.1.287  24 pass  0 fail`, and one wrapped
  start. Every reading is green, and no process is left (`inputs#I3`).

- matrix#v1-01 — Every push produces a run on `ubuntu-latest` whose seven jobs read `verdict: green` on this chunk's
  pushed sha: build, fmt, fatal lint, the tokio-free check, the dependency policy (advisories included), zizmor,
  tests, and perf in its own job. Gate tools are checked present first, homes are kept until G2/G4/the scan
  (`AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`), and the uploads are gated on the secret scan. The last scheduled `nightly.yml` run is
  recorded with its conclusion (ci.py reads; `evidence/ci.md`).

- matrix#v1-03 — The drift contract (`contract_fake_agent_drift`) replays every recorded set green, and a planted change to
  a forwarded `annotations` byte reads `dialog_drift` red. The fixture-hygiene contract refuses a real path, username or
  email (`tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs`).

- matrix#v1-04 — The `run`, `hook`, `mcp` and `cli` roles write schema-true lines under the closed vocabulary (G4
  green). A null correlation is a missing key, the hook writes no stderr and keeps exit 0 on a failed write, and
  `agent-run logs` merges and filters by instance, kind and process with torn lines marked. Each clause is read
  through its named witness; the `ui` role left 0.1.0 by the founder's 2026-10-16 ruling.

- matrix#v1-05 — G2, G4 and the canary secret-scan pass in CI. The print and raw-log bans fire (`lint-probes.sh`,
  clippy), and the forced-panic seam exits 0 with one line. `contract_config_keys` holds the closed key set, with no
  key reaching redaction, and its planted `redact` key is refused.

- matrix#v1-07 — Coverage holds 85/95/80 in `pre-push` and CI `test`, and the five hyperfine rows are under their
  bound (`gate --require perf`). Each of the five security-named parser surfaces (security-plan fct-h4bkgare) has a
  seeded proptest module and a fuzz target whose corpus replay fails on an empty corpus. nextest has `retries = 0`,
  and each job ends in one gate verdict.

- matrix#v1-09 — by construction: `v1-09-amendments.md` names the architecture fact stating each of the five standing
  CLI amendments, and records the three web amendments as having left by the 2026-10-16 ruling.

- matrix#v1-10 — `send-issued` / `send-confirmed` / `send-refused` and the unconfirmable outcome are recoverable from
  `events.ndjson` alone. They do not wake `wait`, and a client-side refusal is visible in `cli-<name>.ndjson`: each
  through its named test, the tests reading the logged records.

- matrix#v1-13 (re-worded, `inputs#I2`: «and MCP» dropped) — Every human output line of `release --budget` and of
  `link` / `unlink` is built from its `--json` result, read by `path6_release_budget_lifts_the_pause` and
  `link_verbs_print_the_design_lines`.

- matrix#v1-24 — The statusline source is named (`statusline-source.json`, else the default home's
  `~/.claude/settings.json`), never written by viola, redirectable per home (`boot --statusline-echo`), and the
  wrapped statusline prints the user's output unchanged (its pass-through witness).

- matrix#v1-26 — manual: `v1-26-fix-pass.md`'s table names X8, X10 and X11 with each one's test read green in this
  chunk's runs, and records X13 as having left 0.1.0 with the page.

title: Linux CI pipeline from the first commit

record.title: Linux CI pipeline from the first commit
record.requirement: every push and PR runs build, format, lint (warnings fatal), the tokio-free check of the sync crates, the dependency policy (licences, C-crate, tokio and banned-crate rules, advisories, sources), workflow linting and tests, natively on Linux; all actions are SHA-pinned under least-privilege permissions; a weekly scheduled advisory check runs without code changes; the perf gates run in their own job; tools the gates need are checked present first and fail loudly if missing; test homes survive until every gate has read them; and nothing from a test home is uploaded unless the secret scan passed.
record.observed_gap: no workspace, no `Cargo.toml`, no `.github/workflows/`; nothing builds or runs in CI (H:91-94). Two masters disagree on CI mechanics: the perf gates' job (tests: own job; obs: inside E2E), `jq`/`rg` availability, where test homes live and whether they survive until the gates, and which artifacts upload after the secret scan (XF F1, F2, B1, B4, B7, Z8).

verification.acceptance: Every push produces a CI run on `ubuntu-latest` whose seven `ci.yml` jobs (test, perf, lint, msrv, fuzz-replay, release, supply-chain) read `verdict: green` on this chunk's pushed sha through `ci.py conclusion`: build, fmt, fatal lint, the tokio-free check of the sync crates, the dependency policy (`cargo deny check` with its advisories family green and no ignore), zizmor and tests; the perf gates run in their own `perf` job; each job checks its gate tools present first; `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1` keeps test homes until G2, G4 and the secret scan have read them; every test-home upload waits on the secret scan; and the last scheduled `nightly.yml` advisory run (no code change) is recorded with its conclusion in the chunk's `evidence/ci.md`.

data.line: - **v1-01** · Linux CI pipeline from the first commit — every push and PR runs build, format, fatal lint, the tokio-free check of the sync crates, the dependency policy, workflow linting and tests natively on Linux under SHA-pinned least-privilege actions, plus a weekly advisory run; perf gates run in their own job, gate tools are checked present first, test homes survive until every gate has read them, and nothing from a test home uploads unless the secret scan passed (per intent F-01; A:431-442; S:303-333; TP §9; OB §9).

## The question, as asked (the recommendation first)

Plan step 10 reads the 3600 s hold on a PERMISSION dialog: the prompt asks the session to run a shell `touch`. But your
user-level ~/.claude/settings.json allows `Bash(*)`, so real claude 2.1.287 auto-allows that command. No

should the wrapped start raise its dialog?

3. **Stop for a re-plan.** Run no live session now. Gates and records continue, and the live round goes back through

title: evidence/live-ledger.py
body:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The one writer of the start ledger (plan.md steps 1, 2, 13 and 15).

It appends one row to `live-sessions.ndjson`: the row is read from a JSON file, parsed and re-serialised, so a
mangled row fails here and never lands, and `written_at` is the UTC time read from the clock at the write, never a
time typed by hand. A `start` row is written before its start is made.

  live-ledger.py <ledger> <row file>

Run from the repository root.
"""
import datetime
import json
import sys


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    ledger, row_file = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    with open(row_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        row = json.load(f)
    if not isinstance(row, dict) or not isinstance(row.get("kind"), str):
        sys.exit("a row is an object with a kind")
    row["written_at"] = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    line = json.dumps(row, sort_keys=False)
    with open(ledger, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(line + "\n")
    print(line)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

title: evidence/live-pty.py
body:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The headless host of a session (plan.md steps 1, 2 and 13; inputs#I4).

It opens a plain pty itself, sets its size to 210 columns by 45 rows, starts the given command on it as the
session leader, and drains the master. The bytes are counted and discarded: no screen is kept. Nothing is
written to the master while the session runs. No compositor, no window, no key of a desktop.

The stop is the form the harness's supervise uses (crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/supervise.rs, `stop`): Ctrl-C
written to the pty, again every 500 ms, until the child exits. It begins when `<private dir>/<label>.stop`
appears or the host gets TERM / INT. A child still alive 10 s into the stop is killed and the status says so.

The command's environment is declared, not inherited: HOME, USER, LOGNAME, SHELL, PATH, LANG, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and
TERM=xterm-256color. No CLAUDE* and no VIOLA* name crosses.

  live-pty.py <private dir> <label> -- <command> [args...]

Status: `<private dir>/<label>.pty.json`, written at the start and again at the end (codes and counts only).
Run from the repository root.
"""
import datetime
import errno
import json
import os
import select
import signal
import sys
import termios
import time

COLS, ROWS = 210, 45
CTRL_C_EVERY = 0.5
STOP_BOUND = 10.0
KEPT = ("HOME", "USER", "LOGNAME", "SHELL", "PATH", "LANG", "XDG_RUNTIME_DIR")


def stamp():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f")[:-3] + "Z"


def declared_env():
    env = {k: os.environ[k] for k in KEPT if k in os.environ}
    env["TERM"] = "xterm-256color"
    return env


def write_status(path, doc):
    tmp = path + ".tmp"
    with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(doc, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    os.replace(tmp, path)


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 5 or sys.argv[3] != "--":
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    priv, label, cmd = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[4:]
    if not os.path.isdir(priv):
        sys.exit("no private directory")
    status = os.path.join(priv, label + ".pty.json")
    stop_file = os.path.join(priv, label + ".stop")
    if os.path.exists(stop_file):
        sys.exit("a stop request for this label already stands")

    master, slave = os.openpty()
    termios.tcsetwinsize(master, (ROWS, COLS))
    env = declared_env()
    pid = os.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        os.close(master)
        os.login_tty(slave)
        try:
            os.execvpe(cmd[0], cmd, env)
        finally:
            os._exit(127)
    os.close(slave)

    doc = {
        "label": label,
        "host_pid": os.getpid(),
        "child_pid": pid,
        "cols": COLS,
        "rows": ROWS,
        "env_names": sorted(env),
        "started_at": stamp(),
        "state": "running",
    }
    write_status(status, doc)

    asked = {"signal": None}

    def on_signal(signum, _frame):
        asked["signal"] = signal.Signals(signum).name

    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, on_signal)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, on_signal)

    drained = 0
    presses = 0
    stop_began = None
    last_press = 0.0
    killed = False
    exit_status = None
    while True:
        try:
            ready, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)
        except InterruptedError:
            ready = []
        if ready:
            try:
                chunk = os.read(master, 65536)
            except OSError as e:
                if e.errno != errno.EIO:
                    raise
                chunk = b""
            drained += len(chunk)
        done, st = os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
        if done:
            exit_status = st
            break
        now = time.monotonic()
        if stop_began is None and (asked["signal"] or os.path.exists(stop_file)):
            stop_began = now
            doc["stop_cause"] = asked["signal"] or "stop-file"
            doc["stop_began_at"] = stamp()
        if stop_began is not None:
            if now - stop_began > STOP_BOUND and not killed:
                killed = True
                try:
                    os.killpg(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                except ProcessLookupError:
                    pass
            elif not killed and now - last_press >= CTRL_C_EVERY:
                try:
                    os.write(master, b"\x03")
                    presses += 1
                except OSError:
                    pass
                last_press = now

    # what the child's group still wrote after its leader was reaped
    while True:
        ready, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.2)
        if not ready:
            break
        try:
            chunk = os.read(master, 65536)
        except OSError:
            break
        if not chunk:
            break
        drained += len(chunk)
    os.close(master)

    doc.update(
        {
            "state": "ended",
            "ended_at": stamp(),
            "drained_bytes": drained,
            "written_before_stop": 0,
            "ctrl_c_presses": presses,
            "killed": killed,
            "exit_code": os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(exit_status),
            "stopped": stop_began is not None,
        }
    )
    write_status(status, doc)
    print(json.dumps({k: doc.get(k) for k in ("label", "state", "exit_code", "killed", "ctrl_c_presses", "drained_bytes", "stopped")}, sort_keys=True))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# The live round (plan steps 8–10): one verify (red), one unverified wrapped start (green readings)

**Status (2026-11-06T20:17Z):** on claude 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host, the verify read **red**
(`stamped 2.1.287  23 pass  1 fail`, row `statusline-rate-limits`) and was not re-fired. The overseer then spent the
cap's second slot on one **unverified** wrapped start (`inputs#I6`, a departure from step 9's «session 2 is not made»).
It read openpty, the start order, the 0700 socket directory and 0600 socket, a clean child fd table, and the
killed-wrapper leg: the child was gone **0.401 s** after its wrapper's SIGKILL. The 3600 s hold was **not read**: an
unverified CLI holds no dialog, so CARRY 2 stays PROVISIONAL.

- Cap (`inputs#I1` item 1, `inputs#I3` «Verify = запасная»): **2 starts of 2**, each ledgered before it was made
  (`live-sessions.ndjson`, `written_at` read from the clock). Reds: 1 (the verify), not re-fired. No third start.
- No key was typed into any dialog or into the session. The rig wrote nothing to its pty (0 Ctrl-C presses, 0 bytes
  written); the wrapped start ended by `kill -KILL` of the wrapper, not by a key.
- Deviations from plan step 10, each on the overseer's technical word (founder-delegated):
  - `inputs#I5` (before the verify): the hold would read a **question** dialog, not a permission dialog. The
    user-level `~/.claude/settings.json` allows `Bash(*)`, so a shell command raises no PermissionRequest on this host.
  - `inputs#I6` (after the red verify): one unverified session 2 instead of none. No `config.json` was written and no
    prompt was sent, because an unverified start holds no dialog.

No prompt text, question text, assistant text, session id, `CLAUDE*` value, pid, absolute path or `detail-*.ndjson`
line is in this file. Times are UTC, read from the clock, on 2026-11-06.

## Setup

- **The rig:** `live-pty.py` and `live-ledger.py`, copied byte for byte from chunk 2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver
  (`rec.py files` first, then `cmp` exit 0 on each). No other rig script was written. Scratch readers outside the tree
  printed codes, counts, booleans and durations only (`live-read.py`, `live-census.py`, `trust.py`, all in the session
  scratchpad).
- **The build:** `cargo build --bin viola` after the gate block's first batch (no fake-agent feature).
  `target/debug/viola` sha256 prefix `69e1a7d92c040450`, read before each session (unchanged between them).
- **Dirs:** `target/done-check-live-20261106T201225Z/` with `vhome/`, `priv/` and `priv/cwd/`, all fresh and 0700, on
  btrfs under `target/` and outside `target/e2e-home/` (no CI upload reaches them).
- **The environment:** every viola verb and the rig ran under `env -i` with `HOME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, `SHELL`, `LANG`,
  `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, and `PATH` with the 2.1.287 install dir first (and `TERM` for the rig): no `CLAUDE*` and no
  `VIOLA*` name. `--home` was always given.
- **Before each session:** `hyprctl locked` false (20:12:45Z, 20:16:18Z); `claude --version` by path
  `2.1.287 (Claude Code)`; census 0 (processes whose exe lies under this repository's `target/`, or whose args name the
  round dir); no `.viola-verify-*` dir at the root.
- **The trust guard:** the start's cwd `priv/cwd/` lies inside the work tree. `~/.claude.json` has no entry for it
  and reads the repository root `trusted`. The CLI 2.1.287 walks from its cwd up to the git root for a trusted entry
  (read in the binary: the walk is bounded by the git root). No trust dialog was expected, and `session-start` came
  within 5 s.

## Session 1: the verify — RED

- Ledgered 20:12:59Z. From the repository root, 20:13:06Z–20:14:06Z (60 s):
  `target/debug/viola --home <vhome> verify -- <claude 2.1.287>`. Exit **1**, stderr empty, stdout ends
  `stamped 2.1.287  23 pass  1 fail`. The failing row: `[21/24] statusline-rate-limits` «the statusline payload carries
  two whole-number rate_limits windows». No `.viola-verify-*` dir was left.
- **The cause, read without a re-fire:** this builder session's own wrapped status line wrote its budget reading 2 s
  before (`budget.json`, read as shapes only): `five_hour` the word `unknown`, and `seven_day` present with a number.
  The account's status-line payload carries one window now, and the row needs two. The row reads the account's plan
  state, not the CLI (`inputs#I6`'s finding).
- Ledgered `reading` (verify-stamp, red) and `census` (0 left) at 20:15:11Z.

## Session 2: the unverified wrapped start — readings green, hold unread

- Ledgered 20:16:32Z. From `priv/cwd/`: `live-pty.py <priv> s2 -- target/debug/viola --home <vhome> run done-check --
  <claude 2.1.287>`, 210×45, started about 20:16:36Z.

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| `session-start` | cause `startup`, within 5 s of the start |
| `events.ndjson` lines 1–3 | `wheel` → `budget-gate` → `session-start` |
| `process-start{subject:"claude-child"}` | 1 line; `pty_backend` **`openpty`**; `cli_version` 2.1.287; `cli_verified` **false** (the red stamp); `env_stripped_count` 0 (nothing to strip under `env -i`); no `CLAUDE*` value key |
| `process-start{subject:"self"}` | 1 line |
| snapshot | `cli_verified` false, `cli_version` 2.1.287, wheel `driver`, endpoint recorded |
| socket directory / socket | **0700** / **0600**, both owned by this user, the socket a socket |
| pinned copy / plugin | the pinned copy is a file under `<vhome>/bin/`; `plugin/<key>/` written at this start |
| wheel lines | 1 (`driver`, cause `start`): no human key |
| the child's fd table (`/proc/<child>/fd`) | 31 fds: pty 7, socket 14, other 10; fds 0–2 all on the pty; **no** socket that is viola's endpoint (its inode found in `/proc/net/unix`) or any socket the wrapper holds; **no** file under the home |
| `parse-rejected` (run) · `panic` (run, hook) | 0 · 0, 0 |

- **The killed-wrapper leg** (CARRY 11's real-claude leg): at 20:16:54.703Z the wrapper and its child read alive by pid
  and start time. `SIGKILL` went to the wrapper after its start time matched. Its child was gone by pid and start time
  **0.401 s** later (bound 10 s). `process-exit{subject:"self"}` lines: **0**, and no child `process-exit` line either.
  The rig saw its child (the wrapper) end with exit code −9 and wrote nothing before it: 0 Ctrl-C presses, not killed by
  the rig, 2 502 bytes drained.
- **The hold — not read:** no prompt was sent and no dialog was raised. On an unverified CLI the wrapper replies `null`
  to a dialog at once (`src/run/dialog.rs:674`), so no hold near 3600 s can be read. Ledgered `reading` (hold,
  `unread`).
- Census after: 0. Ledgered `census` (2 starts, 0 left, 1 red, 1 unread) at 20:17:19Z.

## What the ledger's readers read

The plan's readers (gate entries 37–39) read this ledger: 2 starts (the cap), 0 processes left, and **2 readings not
green** (the verify `red`, the hold `unread`). Entry 39 reads red by construction of this round; its cause is the
verify's row above, never a key or a re-fire.

## After

# T3's witness — «overseer drives a builder through viola» (step 11; `inputs#I2` T3)

This builder session's own wrapping, read at 2026-11-06T20:18Z through the installed product build (the `viola` the
session's wrapper process runs, `~/.local/viola-product/bin/viola`; the session's own `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR`
choose the home). Kinds and counts only: no text, id, path or time. It spends no live start.

finding about the driver's own setup, recorded as measured, and no product fault.

body: - **[Hook Transport] Exec-form `command` hooks: `"command": "<pinned viola copy>", "args": ["hook", "<event>"]`.** Tiers: sync with a decision (PreToolUse `AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode`, PermissionRequest); the sync spine, no reply body, within viola's spine deadline (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop; SessionEnd inside its 1.5 s budget, never raised); async, printing nothing. A lost endpoint loses the event, not the turn. Rationale: exec form skips shell startup.

- **[Hook Contract] Hooks fail open.** Exit 0 with a JSON body is a decision, with no body no decision; exit 2 is never produced, and `hook` never writes to stderr. A sync dialog hook waits at most the dialog hold (`dialog_hold_s`, 60–3600 s, default 60; ceiling PROVISIONAL, owner: 0.2.0's first entry), the dialog then rendering for the human. Rationale: exit 2 blocks Claude Code, and a viola bug must never block the session.

- **[Error Handling] thiserror 2.0.20, one enum per workspace crate; anyhow 1.0.104 only in the `viola` bin.** Ratified exceptions: `viola-pty`'s hand-written `PtyError`, and `viola-mcp`'s `ServeError`, `viola-state`'s `StampsError`, `PinError`, `StampsReadError` and `Refused`; `RefusalReason` lives in `viola-core`. Rationale: callers branch on refusal variants across three surfaces, and anyhow's chains serve only the owner's post-mortem, never a role line, stdout or stderr.

- **[Deployment / Distribution] `cargo install --path .`, with the plugin compiled into the binary (KEYSTONE).** At start `viola run` pins its own exe under `<viola home>/bin/<version>-<hash>/`, refusing a copy that fails its re-hash, and rewrites the plugin for that copy, loaded with `--plugin-dir`; hooks and MCP never search PATH. Rationale: the binary and the plugin can no longer drift apart; the content hash keys the copy because the version alone collides across rebuilds; one tree can build two files whose loaded sections are equal and so key two copies, its cause not explained, known and left without action in 0.1.0, the re-hash the guard.

- **[PTY] portable-pty `=0.9.0` pinned behind viola's own `pty` seam (spawn · read · write · resize · wait · kill).** Child exit is detected on the process handle, never on EOF; `pty_backend()` is `openpty`; viola never holds, queues or re-orders a human key behind a resize and never answers DA1 itself. Rationale: exact, as the workspace pins every third-party version; 0.9.0's graph holds neither `pin-utils` (RUSTSEC-2026-0441) nor the `serial` crate family, and `viola-pty` builds and passes its tests on it unchanged.

One native Rust binary `viola` (Rust 1.98.1, workspace floor 1.96, edition 2024): std threads with Tokio built only inside `mcp`; clap for the CLI; portable-pty `=0.9.0` behind viola's own `pty` seam; vt100 for readiness; interprocess local sockets (JSON-RPC 2.0 over ndjson); ndjson append logs + atomically replaced JSON snapshots, no database, broker, container or hosting; rmcp for the stdio MCP server; GitHub Actions on `ubuntu-latest` against the fake agent.

- **[CLI Conventions] Human text by default, `--json` for agents, a typed exit code per refusal. Prompt text comes from stdin or `--file`, never from a leading-slash argument.** Rationale: agents need machine-parseable refusals.

- **Rust error types:** one error enum per crate, named `<Crate>Error` (`PtyError`, `ChannelError`, `StateError`, `AgentError`, `McpError`), each a `thiserror` enum except `PtyError`, whose `Display`/`Error` are hand-written with fixed messages ([Error Handling]; `viola-mcp`'s `ServeError` beside `McpError`, `viola-state`'s `StampsError` beside `StateError`, `PinError`, `StampsReadError` and `Refused` are the ratified exceptions named there, nine `thiserror` derives over the product sources in all, `crates/viola-e2e` outside the count, by `command grep -rn "thiserror::Error" src crates --include=*.rs`). nutype validation errors fold into the owning crate's enum. `anyhow` appears only in the root bin crate.

- **[PTY] portable-pty `=0.9.0` pinned behind viola's own `pty` seam (spawn · read · write · resize · wait · kill).** Child exit is detected on the process handle, never on EOF. The host stdin handed to the pump is `viola_pty::host_stdin()`, which is `std::io::stdin()`. Its callers are `run`'s pump and the fake agent. Rationale: exact, as the workspace pins every third-party version; 0.9.0's graph holds no `pin-utils`, so RUSTSEC-2026-0441 does not reach the build, and `viola-pty` compiles unchanged on it. `viola run` puts its own host terminal into raw mode for the run through `HostTerminal` (Unix termios) and restores the saved modes on Drop; off a terminal it is a no-op.
 The child's cwd is set explicitly to viola's current directory. A revived start has the one other source: `viola revive` sets the child's cwd to the instance snapshot's recorded `cwd`, the directory the first start spawned its child in. It reads that value only after the strict-modes check on the instance's files, and it must name an existing directory, else the revive is refused `cwd-missing`. Program resolution and the version gate never read the recorded directory: the program is looked up on the reviving process's own `PATH`, from its own current directory (a boundary widening the founder ratified live on 2026-10-10, after it was shown to him as one, the overseer and the operator as relay; chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive). viola resolves the child program to an absolute path itself. The pump keeps the input writer until the child exits. The exit is recorded as `exit_source` `handle-wait` or `kill-fallback`.
 viola never holds, queues or re-orders a human key behind a resize ([Human Takeover / Wheel]). A test that writes a key after a resize waits for the child to observe the new size first.
 `viola_pty::pty_backend()` is always `openpty`, and `viola_pty::host_size()` reads `TIOCGWINSZ`.

- **[Hook Transport] Exec-form `command` hooks: `"command": "<pinned viola copy>", "args": ["hook", "<event>"]`.** Tiers:
  - sync with a decision: PreToolUse with matcher `AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode`, plus PermissionRequest.
  - sync with no reply body (the ordering spine): SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop. Each writes its `hook.event` and exits 0 within viola's spine deadline: one built-in value for every event, below the `timeout` (5 s) those hooks get in `hooks.json`. That value is the product constant `viola_core::SPINE_DEADLINE` = 1 s, the bound the perf gate reads (test-plan §10). The connect deadline `viola hook` passes to `Client::connect_by` is the hook-local, crate-private `CONNECT_DEADLINE` = 750 ms (provisional), asserted below `SPINE_DEADLINE` by a unit test. If the endpoint cannot be reached or written within the deadline, the hook records the failure in `diagnostics/` and exits 0. The event is lost rather than the turn delayed, and a driver recovers through `wait`'s `timeout_ms`.
  - SessionEnd: sync within viola's own ~1 s budget: the channel under the same provisional 750 ms `CONNECT_DEADLINE`, else, once the instance check has passed ([Hook Contract]) and the endpoint is not reached or its server check fails, a direct `try_lock` append (`viola_state::try_append_event` with `Source::Hook`, which writes nothing while `events.ndjson.lock` is held), else nothing; `hooks.json` gives it no `timeout` key. `run` writes `session-end` from the process exit if no hook arrived.
  - `async: true`, printing nothing: Notification, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure.

  Rationale: exec form skips shell startup. `http` hooks need a fixed URL, which means a central listener and so a daemon. `mcp_tool` is unavailable at SessionStart. The 1.5 s SessionEnd budget is never raised. The tier map is itself a ledger row that `viola verify` re-stamps.

- **CLI:** `viola wait` returns `{timed_out:true}` only for a timeout the caller passes in. The MCP `wait` tool (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) clamps its `timeout_ms` to `WAIT_CAP` 50 000 ms, which is also its default when the caller passes none (`viola_mcp::wait_timeout`), so an MCP `wait` with no timeout is answered `timed-out` after 50 s; that bound falls on the driver only (the hidden, plugin-run `viola mcp` serves a driving Claude session, never a person): no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it, and the wheel is untouched. A raised dialog takes a `viola answer` only within the dialog hold (`config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s`, whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, read once at the wrapper's start into `DialogHold`, its bounds `DIALOG_HOLD_MIN` / `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX`, each PROVISIONAL, owner: 0.2.0's first entry; any other value gives 60 and one `parse-rejected`; under the `hooks.json` dialog `timeout` of 3615 s and the hook's own bound `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s`, 3605 s; chunk 2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver); at the hold's end the wrapper replies `null` and appends one `dialog-expired` line (`source: wrapper`, `{dialog_id, dialog_kind}`) that wakes a parked `wait`, the hook exits 0 with no body, the dialog renders for the human in the `claude` TUI, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` / `unknown-dialog` (exit 13) — the hold bounds the driver, never the human: any human key still hands the held dialog back at once, whatever the hold. A `viola send` on a verified CLI waits in the readiness gate for the input box for at most `GATE_MAX_WAIT` (8.5 s, architecture [Screen Model]) and is then refused `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` with nothing typed. That bound falls on the driver only as well: a key pressed during the wait goes to the child and takes the wheel at once, and the waiting send is then refused `human-typing`.
 Once typed, a confirmed `viola send` waits for its confirmation within `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` (10 s), and a `/compact` send on a verified CLI within its own `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (40 s, PROVISIONAL, architecture [Delivery Confirmation]); a send not confirmed inside its window is `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted`. That bound falls on the driver only too: the confirm wait takes no key and blocks, refuses or delays none, and the wheel is untouched. `viola hook statusline` runs the user's own status line command under `STATUSLINE_DEADLINE` (5 s, PROVISIONAL, `src/cmd/hook.rs`) and exits 0 with empty stderr in every case. That bound falls on the user's own command, never on a keystroke and never on the human: no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it, and the wheel is untouched. `viola list` and `viola revive` each make one `claude agents --json` read (a direct spawn, stdout through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`, killed at 5 s; chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board): a failed, oversize, malformed or timed-out read leaves `list`'s board as `board::read` gave it and passes `revive`'s preflight (fail open). That bound falls on viola's own child only, never on a keystroke or the human: no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it. A budget pause is a bound on the driver only as well (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor): while a five-hour or seven-day window stands at or over its threshold (`config.json` `five_hour`, default 90, and `seven_day`, default 85; no value of either switches the gate off) with a known reset still ahead, an automated `viola send` is refused `budget-paused` with detail `five-hour` or `seven-day` (exit 11) and nothing is typed, until that window's reset or a `viola release <name> --budget` for that instance.

- **Agent-mode flag:** **none.** JSON-to-file is the only mode (obs-scope §3).
  - The level comes from `config.json` key `diagnostics_level` (`"info"` default | `"debug"`), applied through a `tracing_subscriber::filter::Targets` layer built in code.
  - It is never read from `RUST_LOG`, and `EnvFilter` / the `env-filter` feature is never enabled.
  - Level changes volume only. Every level uses the same field allow-list, so no setting can disable redaction (security Anti-Patterns).
  - Third-party targets (`rmcp`, `portable_pty`, `sysinfo`, `interprocess`) are `OFF` in every sink, because their records lack the required fields. Their failures are captured at viola's seam from the returned `Result`s (D-11).
  - With `tracing-log` off and no hand-installed `LogTracer`, `log` records from portable-pty `=0.9.0` are dropped; the failure classes they flag are captured from returned values or handles instead: a `pty.spawn` (openpty) spawn failure is an `Err` from the seam and becomes `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"internal-error"}` with the chain in `detail-run.ndjson`; a child exit without EOF is detected by the handle-wait thread (`exit_source`), independent of `log`. The accepted loss is only third-party `log` context emitted without a returned error. The chaos case "child exit without EOF" must find a viola line; one that does not is a seam gap, answered by a seam fix or the researched fallback json-subscriber 0.3.0, never by re-enabling `tracing-log` or installing `LogTracer` (D-11, D-23).

With no `--instance` flag, the instances are `overseer` and `builder`, whatever other flags are given (for example Path 6's `--statusline-echo`). One or more `--instance` flags replace that default list. `--agents-mode` defaults to `recorded`. `--statusline-echo` (built at chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs; clap `conflicts_with` `--unstamped`, the misuse usage `arguments`: the home exists only once step 4's `viola verify` made it) runs after step 4 and before step 5. A `reason:"statusline-source-unresolved"` refusal is dropped: its premise (an unnamed source) is gone, and no entry owes it. `--agents-mode recorded|oversize|malformed` (built at the same chunk; an unknown value is usage `arguments`) writes the fake agent's `agents-mode` file beside the session's `bin/claude` copy, which the fake reads beside its exe; it sets no env var (the founder's own answer to P4 fork 2 of chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board, `inputs#I1`). A stale file is removed before step 4 and the value written (`replace_private`, 0600) after step 4 and the statusline plant, before `supervise.json`: step 4's Run B reads `claude agents --json` through that same copy, so a mode written first failed the `agents-join` row (`verify-failed`, as measured at chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs under `malformed`). It is recorded as `agents_mode` (serde default) in `session.json` and `supervise.json`, so a spec can reproduce the E1 unwrapped row. Steps:

It never builds into the `target/` that the shim's `cargo run` uses: on the retired Windows host a running `target/debug/viola-harness.exe` could not be relinked, and a workspace-wide build re-fingerprints it (measured 2026-09-24: `os error 5`, `UnitDependencyInfoChanged`). On failure it reports `reason:"build-failed"`, and no timeout applies to this step.
  2. Choose the home under the workspace's `target/e2e-home/` (obs-plan §9: CI's zero-panic G2 gate, the G4 schema gate, the secret scan and the `diag-<os>` upload all read `target/e2e-home/**`). Create a unique parent with `tempfile::Builder::new().prefix("viola-session-").tempdir_in("<workspace root>/target/e2e-home")?.keep()` and pass `<parent>/home`, which does **not** exist yet, as `--home`. viola then creates the home itself, 0700. The base `target/e2e-home` itself is prepared before the `tempdir_in` by `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs`): a plain base (absent, or a directory) is created as a directory; on Unix a base that is a link must have an absolute target, which is made with mode 0700 when it is gone (one non-recursive create, never a chmod after, never a parent) and accepted only when one `lstat` reads a real directory with no group or other bit, and refused when its filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`; the message and the floor: §3 Test data bootstrap). A refused base reads `reason:"build-failed"`, the reason a failed create gave before; none was added. On the Linux dev host the base is an operator-set link to the owner-only tmpfs directory `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>` (§5 Setup / teardown lifecycle); the path string is unchanged, and no CI runner has a link.

Unless `--unstamped` is given, run `viola verify --home <home>` against the fake agent driven with `--screens --turn-stop --trusted-root <workspace root> --dialogs --framing`, so its print probe and all five interactive runs (Run A, Run B with its five added compiled pastes — the long, the tag-like and the newline texts, then `/compact`, then `/clear` — the dialog Runs C and D, and Run E, the `--resume` start of Run B's first session) stamp every relied ledger row (`LedgerRow::relied()`: all twenty-four), Run B also making its one `claude agents --json` read (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) and carrying on Unix its one probe `--settings` (`typed/statusline.json`), whose status line the hidden `hook statusline --capture` arm files (the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, relayed verbatim by the operator). | Unit / integration (`ubuntu-latest`) | `std::process::Command` + literal pins; portable-pty outer PTY (cli SGR, tui boundary) | harness `run` JSON `suites[{suite:"nextest-integration"|"nextest-e2e"|"coverage",…,failures[]}]` (CI: `coverage`) | the `test` job's `gate --require coverage,doctest`; no a11y rows, no conformance claim |

- **Surface:** cli (`viola` verbs)
  - **Automated tool reach:**
    - No automated a11y verification tool exists for terminal output; a11y tools assume a DOM or native widget tree.
    - The fallback is output-discipline assertions on the tests' existing CLI drivers: `std::process::Command` on the `viola` binary, the fixed strings pinned by literal in root and unit tests, and SGR-only checks through the portable-pty outer PTY (tests excerpt, E2E driver → cli). Their pass/fail results are machine-parseable through the harness `run` JSON.

    - On Linux alone (the Platform line, below).
    - Orca with GNOME Terminal.
    - Overseer Direction 5: "keyboard and screen-reader discipline, no fake automation".
  - **ARIA roles inventory:** N/A (terminal output). The structural equivalents are:

- **P4 — Human takes the wheel** (tui boundary + cli).
  - **cli:** `send` refused with `human-typing` on stderr, with a typed exit code (`std::process::Command`).
  - **tui:** three portable-pty outer-PTY nextest cases on `ubuntu-latest`, one per Section 1 boundary clause (Section 3 → Keyboard test harness → Tooling): (1) zero viola-originated bytes on the outer-PTY stream, byte for byte against an unwrapped fake-agent run; (2) human keystrokes delivered unblocked past the current atomic paste; (3) `\x1b[I`/`\x1b[O`, mouse and resize sequences do not move the wheel — step-wise (the resize behind its size receipt, then the focus reports with a mouse report as their read barrier), the wheel probed by an `answer` to no pending dialog (exit 13 driver, 10 human), Section 3 → Keyboard test harness → Tooling. A further case sits under clause (2): a key written while a verified `send` waits in the readiness gate takes the wheel, the send exits 10 `human-typing` with nothing typed and the key reaches the child (the same Tooling paragraph, with its stated limit).
  - **SCs:** 2.1.1 (boundary stand-in on tui).

- **Verification:**

- **CLI equivalent (no conformance claim):** amber SGR only on the `DIALOG` word, dim SGR on stale rows and bold SGR only on NAME column values (the callsign; design cli), always beside the word. See `.claude/rules/a11y.md` for path-scoped enforcement.

- **Automated tools per surface:**
  - **web-spa:** none in 0.1.0: the frontend is deferred to 0.2.0 and its technology is not chosen
  - **Mobile:** N/A (phone view deferred)
  - **CLI / TUI:** `std::process::Command` + literal pins + portable-pty outer-PTY output-discipline checks on the `ubuntu-latest` CI leg, Linux only (the frame verbs' server-verify peer pid witness, the socket-directory refusal and the stale-row dim witness `cross_list_rows_dim_a_stale_row_end_to_end_on_a_terminal` among them); manual Orca passes (Linux) supplemental only

1. **a11y-tooling-install** — none in 0.1.0: the cli cases drive the `viola` binary through `std::process::Command`, and the tui cases use the tests' own portable-pty pin; the browser a11y tooling left with the browser leg, and the frontend's is a 0.2.0 input, its technology not chosen

- The a11y harness is the tests' own `std::process::Command` / literal-pin / portable-pty cases (cli output discipline, tui boundary), run by `scripts/agent-run.* run` inside the `test` job's `coverage` suite (matrix `[ubuntu-latest]`) under `gate --require coverage,doctest` (skips never allowed); 0.1.0 runs no browser a11y leg.

- Error enums: one enum per crate named `<Crate>Error` (`PtyError`, `ChannelError`, `StateError`, `AgentError`, `McpError`), each `thiserror` except `PtyError`, whose `Display`/`Error` are hand-written with fixed messages (`viola-pty` takes no thiserror). `viola-agent-claude`'s `AgentError` (crate root) holds `Malformed` (the hook payload), `StampsMalformed` (the stamps envelope) and `resolve_program`'s one refusal, `ProgramNotFound`, with a fixed message. Five ratified exceptions, named in [Error Handling]: `viola-mcp`'s `ServeError` (`Runtime`, `Initialize`, `Session`; fixed messages, returned by `serve`) beside `McpError` (`Internal`, Display `internal error`), `viola-state`'s `StampsError` (`StrictModes`, `State`; fixed messages, returned by `update_stamps`) beside `StateError`, and the three the census adds, `PinError`, `StampsReadError` and `Refused`; nine `thiserror` derives over the product sources in all (arch [Error Handling]).

**What breaks:** 0.9.0's Windows garbage-read bug (wezterm#6783) does not bear on a Linux-only build; the pin is `=0.9.0`, and `viola-pty` builds and passes its tests on it unchanged.
**How to avoid:** keep `=0.9.0` (pinned) behind the `pty` seam; 0.9.0's graph holds neither `pin-utils` (RUSTSEC-2026-0441) nor the `serial` crate family.
**References:** arch [PTY]; security §Data Protection (handle inheritance).

- Ledger rows (S3, S7, S8, R8 identity floor, shim resolution, statusline `rate_limits.*`, the settings-override mechanism and the shell (rows `statusline-override` · `statusline-shell` · `statusline-rate-limits` since chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, relied on every build), harness prefixes, `<pasted_content>` wrapper, modal / input-box signatures, hook tier map, turn end without Stop, dialog concurrency, `claude agents --json` join field (row `agents-join` since chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board: both `pid` and `sessionId` exposed, relied on every build), local commands + post-conditions, tag escaping, largest hook payload) are compiled here, never built from runtime or upstream text.

- `hook` module (as landed): `HookEvent` (9 registered events, the dialog tier `PreToolUse` / `PermissionRequest` included; `from_arg`, `kind()` — an `Option<EventKind>`, `None` for the dialog tier — `is_dialog()`, `as_str` = diag-line `$defs.hook_event`), `normalise(event, bytes) -> Normalised{kind, data, drift}` (Stop's `turn-ended` data is `{last_assistant_message, background_tasks}`: `background_tasks` the payload array's length only, no element read or carried, `null` when the key is absent, `null` or not an array). A wrong-typed known field → a drift entry `{path, expected:"string"}` and read as absent. Prompt order: classify `harness` on the RAW prefix, no trim (`HARNESS_PREFIXES`: `<agent-message from=` / `<task-notification>` / `<\cross-session-message` / `<cross-session-message` — the escaped cross-session form is the one escaped tag that classifies; as measured on 2.1.287 a real cross-session message arrived unescaped under `from` / `from-name` / `from-mode`, and a `<task-notification>` typed at a prompt's very start arrives as typed and is filed `harness`), then unwrap only the CLI's unescaped same-id pair `<pasted_content id="X">\n…\n</pasted_content id="X">` together with the frame the CLI writes around it (the two newlines directly before the open tag, the one directly after the close tag, and a second after it when text follows that is not the next pair's own two-newline frame; a third before, a second after at the prompt's end and a lone one before stay, an unmatched open tag removes nothing; one id serves every pair of a session), then un-escape `<\` before an ASCII letter or `/` — a typed pair is never unwrapped. A pasted text's last newline never reaches the hook (measured on 2.1.287, wrapped or not), so `text` lacks it. No `send` relies on this: `typed_text(text)` returns a sent text with every CR LF pair as one LF, every other CR as one LF, and without its trailing CR and LF characters, every one of them in any order (a `Cow<'_, str>`, borrowed unless an inner CR is replaced; it holds no CR, and nothing else changes: not a TAB, a space, or an LF that is not at the very end), and the root bin's `send` types, classifies and matches that typed text; the client's `refusal_of` is its second product caller (the founder's rulings, 2026-10-07T15:21Z for a trailing LF, 2026-10-09 for a trailing CR and CRLF, 2026-10-09T16:51Z for a CR or a CR LF inside; architecture [Delivery Confirmation]). An LF typed inside a paste is submitted unchanged (as measured on 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-09-inner-cr-and-crlf-in-a-sent-text); every multi-line `send` relies on it, and it is gated by the ledger row `paste-newline` and its `viola verify` probe, Run B's `PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE` (landed at chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row, stamped on live 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host). title: `viola run` wraps the unmodified CLI on Linux

record.title: `viola run` wraps the unmodified CLI on Linux
record.requirement: `viola run <name> -- claude …` shows the child's screen and passes the human's keys exactly as without the wrapper, writing no bytes of its own to the terminal; it resolves the CLI to its real executable, strips the parent session's identity from the child, pins a copy of itself plus a freshly written plugin that hooks call by absolute path, starts in the documented order (collision check … events … child spawn), refuses a name that is already live or stale, and detects child exit on the process, never on end of output.
record.observed_gap: only the prototype hosts `claude` in a ConPTY; the product has no wrapper.

verification.acceptance: One live wrapped start of the unmodified claude 2.1.287 on Linux (the chunk's live round, `evidence/live-round.md`) shows the child's screen with no byte of viola's own on the rig's pty, runs with `process-start{subject:"claude-child", cli_verified:true, pty_backend:"openpty"}` and names only (no values) in its strip fields, calls a pinned copy through a freshly written plugin by absolute path, follows the start order `wheel` → `budget-gate` → `session-start`, and detects the child's exit on the process handle at the killed-wrapper leg; each clause also has its fake-agent witness green in this chunk's runs (the collision and stale-name refusals, the no-EOF exit, `tests/tui_passthrough.rs`).

title: Linux CI pipeline from the first commit

record.title: Linux CI pipeline from the first commit
